summary: Recorded the snapshot-enabled outcome from the previous turn's run in the parent account (violated/asserted, five receipts, gap-2 resolved on both halves) and pursued the registered child question by source trace. The parent interpretation now states the three witnessed consequences with their same-run controls: a replica that already accepted the StopSign and receives a resume point covering it ends one index past its content (follower after reconnected(), follower re-promising in an ordinary new term, the leader that takes over from such a follower, and two followers under a snapshot-capable entry type), a write quorum of inflated reports makes the leader decide the reported index past its own content (NoSnapshot event 24, snapshot-enabled event 53), and the corruption propagates across authority changes; the indexed behaviours and the applicability fact are re-conditioned on both entry configurations, and the limitations now say the snapshot branch is evaluated but not entered and that compaction calls themselves remain unexercised. For the child question (whether a newly elected leader holds the entries up to the decided index it adopts) the trace found that handle_majority_promises pairs two independently ordered inputs — the log from the strictly greatest (n_accepted, accepted_idx) promise and the decided index from the greatest reported decided index over all promises — with no clamp in the leader path, unlike the follower path's update_decided_idx_and_get_accepted_idx; a behaviour records that adoption, and the child interpretation is unresolved with defect_claim unresolved, stating the reachability argument as the protocol invariant the code relies on rather than as a witnessed disagreement, and listing the absence of an execution and of a constructed disagreement history as limits. No execution was requested this turn. Incomplete: that disagreement history and its probe, loss- and timer-triggered re-synchronization, larger clusters, persistence across restarts, and compaction calls.
